newsitem.title: USA: Mexican debt leads Brady market higher on buyback.
newsitem.headline: Mexican debt leads Brady market higher on buyback.

text.p: Mexico led the emerging debt market higher amid the presumption the country bought back Brady bonds with proceeds from a global bond, traders said.

The price of Mexican discount bonds rose on Wednesday morning after news broke late on Tuesday that the government would use its $1.0 billion global bond to replace $1.24 billion face value of discounts.

"The market was very well bid both on this new 20 year bond and on the story that the Mexican government has or would continue to buy back this big block of discounts," said one Brady trader at a large U.S.investment bank.
Mexican finance ministry officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
Brady traders said the global paper due 2016 had tightened six-seven basis points from its issuance. Mexican Pars gained 3/8 to 68-7/8, while discounts rose 5/8 to 84-5/8.
"In an otherwise lackluster market, that is a very good sign for Mexico," said one trader at a large European bank.
Mexico had priced the 20-year global bonds to yield 11.51 percent with a spread 445 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries via Goldman Sachs and Merrill Lynch International.

"As it should, the market has taken very positively the 20 year global bond issue," said Carlos Asilis, senior Latin American economist at Oppenheimer & Co. "This issue is very positive not only because of the tenor, but also because of the spreads which compare so favorably with the global bond issue earlier this year."

Mexico had issued 30-year global bonds in May at 552 basis points over Treasuries. Given the country's success at selling paper to U.S. investors, analysts said the Brady market should expect further attempts to retire collateralized Bradies from Mexico and other emerging debtors.
"If you look at the stripped yield spread compared with where they were able to issue new debt, it still may be attractive to continue this," the debt strategist said.
Debt trade across the emerging market was thin on Wednesday with players operating cautiously ahead of next week's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy making board.
Argentine FRBs edged up 1/8 to 82-3/4, but while Brazilian C bonds climbed 5/8 to 68-7/8.

"It should really not come as a surprise for the markets because that is what these countries are going to do," one fund manager said. "All of them are engaging in better liability management, which they need to do."
